claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at the time of decision, on an unresolved-risk basis rather than a proven control failure.
specific_concerns: The policy requires a material unresolved risk, but the packet summary does not establish materiality with enough specificity.
The cited facts appear to support follow-up or escalation more directly than outright rejection.
Procurement's documented recommendation is conditional follow-up before approval if the issue remained unresolved; that is weaker than an express recommendation to reject.
The packet appropriately avoids claiming a confirmed control failure, but it still relies on cumulative inference from limited summarized evidence rather than a clearly logged reject-level predicate.
Because evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, the admissible record cannot be independently checked for context, timing, or whether the inconsistency was later resolved.
unsupported_claims: Any stronger claim that the record proves a confirmed storage-control failure.
Any claim that the vendor was rejectable solely because of an informal quality process or a single prior quality lapse.
Any implication that private security-review results support rejection unless those results were formally logged.
evidence_requests: The underlying text of BPROC-034-B through BPROC-034-E, including dates and exact wording.
Any formal materiality assessment tying the unresolved storage-controls issue to a reject-level risk standard.
Any approval workflow or procurement policy language showing when unresolved diligence issues require rejection rather than follow-up or conditional hold.
Evidence that the storage-controls inconsistency remained unresolved at the actual decision time.
Any logged decision memo explaining why cumulative concerns crossed the threshold from escalation to rejection.
decision_criteria: Reject only if admissible evidence shows a material unresolved due-diligence risk.
Do not treat questionnaire inconsistencies or quality-process gaps alone as proof of a reject-level control failure.
Do not rely on private security-review results unless they were formally logged.
A compliant rejection requires a clear support link from the cited evidence to the policy threshold, not just general concern.
If the record shows only a need for follow-up before approval, rejection is not fully supported without an additional materiality basis.
